findings.description: AWS access key and secret key are stored in plaintext in the Lambda's environment variables and committed to source control. These credentials are visible to anyone with read access to the Lambda configuration or the Terraform code, and are not encrypted using KMS, exposing sensitive secrets and enabling credential theft.

The Lambda function does not specify a kms_key_arn to encrypt environment variables at rest, meaning sensitive values (such as the embedded credentials) are stored in a less protected state, relying only on default AWS-managed encryption without customer-managed key control.
The function uses nodejs12.x, a deprecated and end-of-life Node.js runtime that no longer receives security patches, increasing exposure to unpatched vulnerabilities.
